source.title: Unified View of Grokking, Double Descent and Emergent Abilities: A Perspective from Circuits Competition
source.authors: Yu-Fei Huang; Sheng-Ding Hu; Xu Han; Zhi-Yuan Liu; Mao-Song Sun

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains models on modular addition and evaluates training and validation accuracy, directly testing grokking with the same general task and measures while varying model and dataset size.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own modular-addition training and validation results, including delayed generalization, dataset/model-size sweeps, and parameter-norm trends. It also reports results from a mixed algorithm-and-memorization task, recorded under fits_no_version. Claims about other work in the related-work section are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Trains the standard 1-layer transformer on (a+b) mod 113 with AdamW and reports train and validation accuracy over epochs. It sweeps dataset size and model size and finds grokking, semi-grokking and memorization-only regimes. These results bear on V1 and on V5's critical-dataset-size prediction. It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors propose that competition between memorization and generalization circuits, with the regime set by model size and data size, unifies grokking, double descent and emergent abilities. They confirm two predictions about when double descent occurs. The link to LLM emergent abilities is offered as a hypothesis from toy multi-task experiments. They note the study is limited to algorithmic tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition and train/validation accuracy, but expands the setup through model-size and dataset-size sweeps and mixed-task experiments; it does not report an exact reproduction of the original training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with model hidden size and training dataset size; the progression trajectory varies across random seeds. The mixed-task experiment also varies memorization-data volume and model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a random-label memorization task delays modular-addition generalization until models are about 1570x larger; splitting the FFN between the two tasks lowers this to about 787x.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Competing memorization load can turn an algorithmic task into an emergent ability with model scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Final validation accuracy against model size shows double descent at small training-set sizes, and this is more pronounced for the harder (a+b)^2 mod P task (Fig. 6, Fig. 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-wise double descent arises from moving between memorization-only and grokking regimes.

record.problems: The experiments are limited to algorithmic tasks and small transformer setups; many trajectories are presented graphically, and the study does not manipulate weight decay to establish the proposed low-norm causal mechanism. The mixed-task experiment reports the highest validation accuracy across three runs rather than a mean.

untested.parts: How the training-step delay scales with dataset size; only final accuracy against dataset size is reported.
Causal role of weight decay (never varied); ungrokking in Varma's sense, i.e. retraining a grokked net on a smaller set.
No circuit tracking or progress measures.
No non-algorithmic data; no manipulation of initialization or norm.
No LLM training on realistic data.
Algorithms are not compared across runs.
Optimizer and numerics are not controlled; AdamW is used throughout.

missing.what: Progression runs (hidden 8, 3000 samples) show the parameter norm rising as generalization appears, the opposite of the grokking runs. This contrast bears on V5's low-norm account.
(a+b)^2 mod P task at 3000 samples: semi-grokking and zero validation at hidden 24, showing the critical dataset size shifts upward with task difficulty.
Memorization capacity grows with model size, measured on random-label training (Fig. 4). This is the assumption behind the regime boundaries.
Semi-grokking interval spans about 1000 training points for all models; hidden 64 semi-groks at 2000–3000 samples.

record.verdict_notes: The paper uses 'ungrokking' for a model that never generalizes when trained from scratch below the critical size, not Varma et al.'s reversion of an already-grokked network; verdicts treat these as different. The weight-decay mechanism is assumed (AdamW chosen because weight decay matters) and never manipulated. The multi-task rows report the best of three seeds.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports delayed generalization and varies dataset size, but does not quantify how the training-step delay changes as the training set shrinks.
It does not identify or track a generalizing circuit or memorizing components over training, nor measure continuous progress indicators that anticipate a jump.
No non-algorithmic image, text, or molecule dataset is tested, and initialization scale or weight norm is not varied to switch grokking on or off.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
The study examines grokking-related dataset/model-size patterns and parameter norms, but does not manipulate weight decay or establish that a low-norm bias causally produces the reported transitions.
The study does not compare whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
The study does not control or compare adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax effects.

rows.subject: 1-layer simplified decoder-only transformer, hidden size 64
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition and report training and validation accuracy over training.
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy during training
rows.value: Models quickly achieve perfect training accuracy; validation accuracy grows up long after training accuracy is perfect, with near-perfect validation accuracy reported for this setting.
rows.uncertainty: not stated for this individual curve
rows.note: The text identifies this as grokking; the figure shows the training trajectory.
rows.check: A single grokking curve (hidden 64, 3000 samples) shows the V1 delay. It carries no information on V5's critical dataset size or weight decay, so the V5 link is removed.

rows.subject: models with hidden sizes 32 and 64
rows.operation_detail: Vary modular-addition training dataset size and compare final validation accuracy across model sizes.

conditions.value: 2,000 to 4,000 in increments of 200; examples highlighted at 3,000 and 4,000

rows.measure: Final validation accuracy; whether near-perfect validation is reached
rows.value: The hidden-size-64 model achieves near-perfect validation accuracy with 3,000 training samples; the hidden-size-32 model requires 4,000 for similar validation accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: Average performance is reported; Figure 3 shows 95% confidence intervals.
rows.note: This supports a smaller critical dataset size for the larger model. It does not quantify training-step delay across dataset sizes.

rows.subject: models with varied hidden sizes
rows.operation_detail: Vary model hidden size on modular addition and compare training and validation accuracy.
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy across model sizes
rows.value: The models pass through progression, ungrokking, and semi-grokking; hidden sizes 24 to 40 have zero validation performance in the ungrokking phase. The text says grokking does not happen in this model-size range.
rows.uncertainty: Mean accuracy and 95% confidence intervals are reported in Figure 6.
rows.note: The reported dynamics include a region without grokking, followed by semi-grokking; the text attributes the absence of grokking in this size range to the small training set.
rows.check: At 2600 samples, hidden sizes 24–40 memorize fully with zero validation and no model in the range groks. This matches V5's prediction that generalization fails below the critical dataset size. 'Ungrokking' here means failure from fresh training, not a grokked network reverting, and V1's delay is not measured, so the V1 link is removed.

rows.subject: models with varied hidden sizes
rows.size_stated: hidden sizes 4 to 100, specified sequence in Section 4.2
rows.operation_detail: Vary model hidden size on modular addition and compare training and validation accuracy.
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy across model sizes
rows.value: The text reports progression, semi-grokking, and grokking, with a validation-performance dip at hidden sizes 28 to 36; it also describes model-wise grokking for smaller training datasets.
rows.uncertainty: Mean accuracy and 95% confidence intervals are reported in Figure 6.
rows.note: The text says smaller training datasets can yield near-perfect validation accuracy long after training accuracy in terms of model size; it does not report training-step delay by dataset size.
rows.check: At 3000 samples, larger models grok and models near the critical size semi-grok, with a validation dip at hidden 28–36. The quoted 'model-wise grokking' is over model size, not training steps.

rows.subject: models with varied hidden sizes
rows.size_stated: hidden sizes 4 to 100, specified sequence in Section 4.2
rows.operation_detail: Vary model hidden size on modular addition and compare training and validation accuracy.
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy across model sizes
rows.value: Models bypass ungrokking and semi-grokking and transition from progression to grokking, with validation performance improving consistently as model size increases.
rows.uncertainty: Mean accuracy and 95% confidence intervals are reported in Figure 6.
rows.note: The paper reports no double-descent pattern for this setting.

rows.subject: 1-layer simplified decoder-only transformer, hidden size 8
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition and report training and validation accuracy over training.
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy during training
rows.value: In progression, the model first memorizes part of the training data without improving validation performance, then improves both training accuracy and validation performance; progression varies across seeds.
rows.uncertainty: Five seed curves are shown; no numerical uncertainty stated.
rows.note: This is a contrasting training dynamic: generalization begins while training accuracy is still increasing, rather than only after perfect training accuracy.
rows.check: Small models that cannot memorize all the data (hidden 8) show 'progression': validation rises before training accuracy saturates. This is the V1 pattern absent in that regime, not a measurement problem.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3, Progression and Discussion; Figures 2(a) and 5.

rows.subject: 1-layer simplified decoder-only transformer, hidden size 64
rows.operation_detail: Measure parameter norm during modular-addition training.
rows.value: Parameter norm decreases as generalization circuits become established.
rows.note: The paper reports the norm trend, but does not manipulate weight decay or directly establish that lower norm causes the transition.
rows.check: The parameter norm falls as generalization forms during grokking (Fig. 9b), consistent with the low-norm account. This is correlational and weight decay is never varied; state changed from partial because the trend itself appears in full.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix A; Figure 9(b) and caption; TAKEAWAY-4.

rows.subject: transformer models trained on modular addition plus a pure memorization task
rows.size_stated: 1-layer hidden size 64 to 8-layer hidden size 1024; model parameters shown in Figure 8
rows.operation_detail: Train jointly on modular addition and random-label subtraction data, varying model size and memorization-data volume.
rows.measure: Validation accuracy on modular addition across model sizes
rows.baseline: Single addition task; exact baseline value not stated
rows.value: The paper reports substantial validation performance at model sizes about 1570 times larger than when training solely on the algorithm task, and says memorization-data volume has minimal impact on the emergent model size.
rows.uncertainty: The highest validation accuracy for each configuration is reported; no numerical uncertainty stated.
rows.note: This is an induced mixed-task emergence result, not a test of grokking on non-algorithmic data or realistic large-model pretraining.

rows.subject: dense and sparse transformer models trained on modular addition plus a pure memorization task
rows.operation_detail: Partition the feed-forward layer to allocate separate sections to modular-addition and memorization data, and compare with dense and single-task models.

conditions.value: sparse model with separately allocated feed-forward sections

rows.measure: Model size at which modular-addition validation accuracy emerges
rows.baseline: Dense multitask model and single addition task; exact values not stated
rows.value: Figure 10 labels the sparse model as 787x larger and the dense model as 1570x larger; the authors state that the sparse design significantly accelerates emergence.
rows.note: The result is about induced emergence in a mixed-task setup; the figure does not provide a numerical validation-accuracy value in the text.

relationships.condition: Modular addition, models able to memorize all training data, with enough data (hidden 32–64 at 3000–4000 samples; large models at 3000–5000)
relationships.reason: Training accuracy is perfect within a few epochs and validation reaches near-perfect long afterwards (r1, r2, r4, r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Models reached perfect training accuracy within a few epochs and near-perfect validation accuracy much later.

relationships.condition: Small models whose memorization capacity is below the training-set size (e.g. hidden 8, 3000 samples)
relationships.reason: Generalization starts before training accuracy saturates ('progression'), so there is no delay beyond overfitting; the pattern also varies across seeds (r7).
relationships.display_finding: Generalization began before training accuracy saturated, with the pattern varying across seeds.

source_check.condition: Small models whose memorization capacity is below the training-set size (e.g. hidden 8, 3000 samples)
source_check.reason: Generalization can emerge at moderate training accuracy when the model cannot memorize all training data; progression varies across seeds (r7). This qualifies the conditions for the delayed-after-saturation pattern.

relationships.condition: Modular addition dataset × model-size sweeps; parameter-norm trajectories during grokking
relationships.reason: Below the critical size models memorize with zero validation; near it they semi-grok; above it they grok; the norm falls during grokking (r2, r3, r4, r8).
relationships.display_finding: Below the critical dataset size, models memorized with zero validation accuracy; near it they semi-grokked, and above it they grokked as norms fell.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Modular addition dataset × model-size sweeps; parameter-norm trajectories during grokking
source_check.reason: Dataset and width sweeps show memorization-only, semi-grokking and grokking regimes, and parameter norm decreases during grokking (r2,r3,r4,r8). These support threshold behavior and are consistent with low-norm selection; causal efficiency and reduced-data retraining are untested.

relationships.reason: The critical dataset size is not one value: it falls from about 4000 (hidden 32) to about 3000 (hidden 64). The critical size therefore depends on model size (r2).
relationships.display_finding: The critical dataset size fell from approximately 4000 samples at hidden size 32 to approximately 3000 at hidden size 64.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: The width-dependent threshold is supported by r2, but V5 does not assert a universal threshold independent of model size. Approximately 4000 samples at hidden size 32 versus 3000 at hidden size 64 is compatible with its critical-size prediction.
